system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING

PHYSICS CHECK — governing physical relation is heat transfer coefficient (U) equation: 1/U = 1/h_shell + R_fouling + 1/h_tube. Fouling resistance (R_fouling) increases over time, reducing U. The calculated rate of back-pressure rise (0.5 kPa/week at fouling onset) must be detectable above measurement noise (±0.1 kPa) and process fluctuations (±0.3 kPa).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — off-the-shelf: existing steam flow meter (FT), existing condensate temperature sensor (TT), existing turbine back-pressure transmitter (PT). Calculation: daily moving average of (steam flow × (saturated temp - actual condensate temp)) / (steam flow × log-mean temp difference). No new components; only existing signal processing.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — standard practice is periodic offline tube cleaning; this approach adds only computational burden to existing control system. Operability and maintenance unchanged; cost class is minimal (software-only) versus standard practice's lost generation during cleaning. Worth it by enabling cleaning scheduling before performance loss.

EXECUTABLE TEST — protocol: monitor calculated indicator daily for 90 days while recording actual back-pressure. Instruments: existing DCS data logs for steam flow, condensate temp, back-pressure. Pass/fail: indicator must show statistically significant increasing trend (p<0.05) at least 21 days before back-pressure reaches 101.3 kPa (derating limit). Duration: 90-day test period covering multiple fouling cycles.
